summary.text: Juliana Stratton is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and the sitting Lieutenant Governor of Illinois. A Chicago attorney and mediator who worked on criminal justice policy in Cook County, she served one term in the Illinois House before being elected lieutenant governor alongside J.B. Pritzker in 2018. She won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 40.4% of the vote.

paragraphs.text: Born in Chicago on September 8, 1965, and raised in the Pill Hill neighborhood on the city's South Side. She attended Kenwood Academy.
Earned a bachelor's degree in broadcast journalism from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1987 and a J.D. from DePaul University College of Law in 1992.

Worked as a video producer for the city of Chicago, then as an attorney; in 1997 she founded JDS Mediation Services and served as an arbitrator and administrative law judge for several City of Chicago agencies.

Taught conflict management and negotiation at Loyola University Chicago, and was executive director of the Cook County Justice Advisory Council (2011-2014) and director of the Center for Public Safety and Justice at the University of Illinois at Chicago (2015-2017).
Won the 2016 Democratic primary for the Illinois House's 5th District, defeating incumbent Ken Dunkin with 68% of the vote, and served in the House from 2017 to 2019.
Was announced in August 2017 as J.B. Pritzker's running mate and was elected Lieutenant Governor in November 2018, taking office in January 2019. She and Pritzker were re-elected in 2022.

As lieutenant governor, she launched the Justice, Equity, and Opportunity Initiative and chairs the Illinois Council on Women and Girls and several other state councils, according to Wikipedia's account.

Announced her U.S. Senate campaign in April 2025 after Sen. Dick Durbin said he would not seek re-election, and won the Democratic primary over U.S. Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly and others.
